profile.campus: Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon (QTS Hillsboro 2 campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own Hillsboro 2 campus page and a corroborating datacentermap DC3 listing, this building sits at 4327 NE Huffman St, Hillsboro, OR 97124, part of the shared 51-acre, 180+ MW, four-building Hillsboro 2 campus.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. Hillsboro, in Oregon's Washington County, is one of three QTS campuses in the immediate area (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3) and part of the Portland metro's broader "Silicon Forest" data center cluster, drawing power from the regional grid and, per QTS's own Hillsboro 3 materials, offering customers 100% renewable energy through power purchase agreements.

Hillsboro's "Silicon Forest" data center cluster grew out of the area's legacy semiconductor and electronics manufacturing base (anchored historically by Intel's large Washington County campuses), which left behind substantial fiber infrastructure and a skilled technical workforce that later attracted data center operators; the Hillsboro Herald, a local outlet, has reported on the scale of competing data center construction projects in the immediate area as the industrial land base has shifted from chip fabrication toward digital infrastructure. QTS's Hillsboro presence, spread across three separate campuses (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3), reflects a broader industry pattern in Oregon's Washington County of sequential campus expansion by the same operator as adjacent land becomes available, similar to the multi-campus patterns seen for QTS in Northern Virginia and for other operators in this registry's Loudoun County and Quincy, Washington clusters. Washington County's land-use and tax-incentive framework for data centers has been debated locally as the industry has grown.

reading.body:
QTS Hillsboro 2 is one of four buildings on a 51-acre campus in Washington County, Oregon with 180 MW of total power capacity. This specific building's individual capacity is not published. Assuming 40 kW per rack at typical AI training density, the full 180 MW campus could hold roughly 4,500 racks, but the building-level split across the four structures is not disclosed, so the portion relevant to this facility cannot be determined from published sources.

The campus ranks ninth among Oregon's eight facilities with published power specifications, meaning its 180 MW total would place it in the state's top tier if attributed to a single facility, though it is actually distributed across four buildings. Oregon has mapped 133 total data centers but only eight have published megawatt figures, making the Hillsboro 2 campus one of very few sites in the state with disclosed capacity. The facility sits in the Portland metro region's "Silicon Forest," an industrial area anchored by legacy semiconductor manufacturing that has since shifted toward digital infrastructure, with competing data center operations from Digital Realty, Verizon, and others.

QTS operates three separate Hillsboro campuses (numbered 1, 2, and 3) in Washington County, a pattern of sequential multi-campus expansion by a single operator that mirrors strategies in Northern Virginia and Washington state. The operator is privately held by Blackstone following a $10 billion acquisition completed in August 2021 and no longer files public capacity disclosures. The campus materials state it can serve customers with 100 percent renewable energy through power purchase agreements, though the binding constraint on this site's ability to scale remains the regional grid connection capacity, which is not published.
